kind: A screen by slope over data on the test bed, two seeds on the server and a third on the laptop: whether cells with a wide proportional gate, under the pool that lifts the ceiling, learn late better than plain cells under the same pool.
why: The Transformer's unit multiplies a gate by a value, and v15's priced walk put plain units in place of gated ones as the largest step from the Transformer to the stack (0.025, docs/STREAM_FORM.md). Every spike form of the gated unit has failed so far: the shunting gate trails the plain bed by 0.108 at 24,000 updates and its deficit grows with data (gated_cells_with_data.json), the self-gated cell is level, and the multiplying forms ran away. A design check (proportional_gate_check.json) found one law that is stable and level with its plain base at 2,250 updates where the shunting gates were 0.063 to 0.080 behind: a gate whose k spikes let in k / 64 of the value dendrite's charge, wide open at 16 thresholds of its own charge, with its steps inside the cell (they send no pulse, as a dendritic spike does not), under the lifting pool, which divides the gate's and the value's charge before any bound so that a loud stream closes gates. A unit's advantage may show only late, where plain cells stop gaining (gap_with_data.json), so the gate is read by its slope from 6,000 to 24,000 updates.

arms.pg16: --granule-gate 4 --granule-ramp 16 --granule-inner-gate --pool-lifts-ceiling: every cell has a signed value dendrite and a gate dendrite with synapses of its own; the gate fires 4 steps for every threshold of its charge above the rest, at most 64, and k steps let k / 64 of the value's charge into the body; on the server's fan2 bed 408 cells a level (--granule-fan 512 --granule-cells 408, 5,239,232 parameters, 6,246 fewer than the base), on the laptop's bed 681 cells a level (--granule-cells 681, 5,245,478 parameters, 3,582 fewer)

base.server: the runs ending in -base: the fan2 bed under the lifting pool, --granule-fan 512 --granule-cells 681 --pool-lifts-ceiling, 5,245,478 parameters, trained here with the same seeds and lengths
base.laptop: lift-6k-s3 and lift-24k-s3 of lifted_gates_with_data (--pool-lifts-ceiling on the laptop's bed, 1,022 cells, 5,249,060 parameters), queued there and trained as that study records

runs.server: pg-24k-s1-base, pg-24k-s1-gate, pg-24k-s2-base, pg-24k-s2-gate, then pg-6k-s1-base, pg-6k-s1-gate, pg-6k-s2-base, pg-6k-s2-gate: seeds 20001 and 20002, through sched/bin/bed.sh stack with --lr 1.2e-3 (and --steps 6000 for the short runs), code v17o (26198b3); pinned to GPU 0 at priority 2, one at a time beside the full-size run there
runs.laptop: pg-6k-s3-gate and pg-24k-s3-gate: seed 20003, the laptop runner's recipe with --lr 1.2e-3, on the frozen copy of 26198b3 (checkpoints/laptop-loop/code-26198b3), after the queue's earlier runs, paired with lift-6k-s3 and lift-24k-s3

training: the delayed test bed's recipe (6 levels, 256 channels, reads after every level, four delays on the reads' and cells' fibres, trained on streams of 10 windows in 3 groups, batch 16 of 256 bytes, warmup 300, cosine over the run, rotated optimizer, averaged weights 0.999, pulse budget 113,000), peak rate 1.2e-3, 6,000 and 24,000 updates
measure: experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, averaged weights, bits of every piece kept; each arm paired with the base of its seed and length; experiments/gap_by_piece.py splits each lead by what the context offers (near 240, far 8,192); the trainer's pulses a byte; the share of gate and cell entries at their caps (experiments/membrane_saturation.py)
reading: The server's two seeds are read by experiments/read_lead_study.py's shared reading: pg16 is a fix for late learning if at 24,000 updates its mean lead over the base is at least 0.010 with both seeds ahead, and its mean lead at 24,000 updates is at least 0.005 larger than at 6,000; a lead at 24,000 without that growth is a constant gain; anything else fails. The laptop's seed, on the other bed shape, is reported beside and does not change the verdict. A fix or a constant gain of at least 0.010 sends the proportional gate to full size under the lifting pool against the lifted plain stack, in a record of its own written before that run. Recorded either way: every lead, the leads on new contexts, the pulses a byte and the gates at their caps.
seen_before_recording: Everything of proportional_gate_check.json, on the laptop's bed at seed 20003 and rate 1.2e-3, over the first 2,250 updates of the 24,000-update schedule. Under the lifting pool: the plain base at 2.0606, 1.7889 and 1.7105 after 750, 1,500 and 2,250 updates, which is also the start of a run like lift-24k-s3; this study's gate at 1.9730, 1.7755 and 1.7072, which is the start of its laptop run pg-24k-s3-gate (same seed, rate, schedule and code); the narrow ramp at 2.3092, 2.4374 and 2.9552; the shunting gate with inner steps at 1.9890, 1.8254 and 1.7736; and the diagnostics of those four runs at 2,250 updates. Under the bounded pool: the shunting gate with inner steps and both ramps, with their diagnostics. Before that: both arms of gated_cells_with_data at 6,000 and 24,000 updates; the pulse split of rd-base-24k-s3, gate-24k-s3 and self-6k-s3; the drive of plain cells and shunting gates in trained and untrained beds (scratch measurements). The server's two fan2 settings trained 2 updates on the CPU as a launch check (finite; 5,245,478 and 5,239,232 parameters). No run on the server's fan2 bed under the lifting pool at rate 1.2e-3, and nothing at 6,000 or 24,000 updates of this gate, has been seen.

result.verdict: FAIL: the proportional gate is behind its base on both seeds at both lengths, by 0.065 and 0.048 bits a byte at 6,000 updates and by 0.802 and 0.653 at 24,000, where a lead of 0.010 was asked. The full-size run (fs-pg6-lift, full_size_proportional_gate.json) stays held and is not run.
result.reading: The gate does not learn late: it comes apart with data. Both long runs still improve at 6,000 updates (1.78 and 1.75 on the trainer's streams, 0.11 and 0.07 behind their bases) and worsen from there to 2.24 and 2.09, while the bases fall to 1.42 and 1.43. Three things move together. The range rule, which shrinks a neuron whose synapses could sum past what the arithmetic holds exactly, starts to act between 6,000 and 12,000 updates and ends at 13,795 and 9,097 neurons; the bases never need it. The stream's neurons fire twice as much (39,000 and 36,600 pulses a byte after reads and cells against 18,000), and under the same budget the output is left with 8,500 and 9,700 pulses a byte where the bases spend 43,000. And the gates stop being graded: at 6,000 updates an open gate lets in 0.57 to 0.74 of its value and 37% to 60% of the open gates stand in the top quarter; at 24,000 updates it lets in 0.82 to 0.87 and 73% to 81% stand in the top quarter, while fewer gates open at all (16% to 39% of cell-bytes, from 36% to 46%). With data the proportional gate turns into the switch that failed before, and the synapses that grow to make it one are what the range rule then cuts. It is not a blow-up at the peak rate: it begins when the rate has already fallen to between 86% and 70% of its peak. Nothing is at a cap either: at most 0.06% of the cell entries, 0.11% of the other entries and 0.01% of the reads' reach theirs in any of the eight runs, so this is not the saturation that the lifting pool removed. The loss is on every kind of context but one: on bytes whose context ran before with another follower (5.5% of bytes) the gated bed is better, by 0.43 and 0.46 at 6,000 updates and by 4.4 and 4.5 at 24,000, as a model with flatter predictions is. The gate's cost beside the score: 34,000 to 45,000 inner steps a byte that the budget does not count, and 3% more time. Not tried: a lower rate for the gate's synapses, a bound or a decay on its drive, a resting level that holds the gates half open. Every spike form of the gated unit has now failed on the bed (shunting 0.108 behind, self-gated level, proportional 0.73 behind) and at full size (shunting 0.113 to 0.118 behind, self-gated level); whether the gated unit earns anything at this size even without spikes is what the float diagnostic of plain and gated units measures (plain_units_with_data.json, running).
